A1.justification: Both are readable 14-page versions of the same SageAttention work. All text, equations, tables, figures, and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-kernel benchmarks, model evaluations, quantization analyses, and ablations in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including throughput comparisons, end-to-end accuracy measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the loaded key/value block indices from i to j inside the j loop, matching the subsequent multiplications already present in v1. This is a localized correction to the written algorithm; smoothing, quantization, accumulator choices, and adaptive selection are unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same language, image/video generation, and image-classification coverage: WikiText, LAMBADA, MMLU, Open-Sora prompts, COCO, ImageNet, ImageNet-Sketch, and ImageNet-R.

E2.justification: Figures 6–9 retain Torch, xformers, and FlashAttn2. Table 1 retains quantized FlashAttn3 and the same quantization alternatives; the full-precision and within-method comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported protocols retain RTX4090/RTX3090 benchmarks, head dimensions 64/128, sequence lengths 1K–32K, and causal/noncausal settings. Evaluation metrics, zero-shot tasks, normally distributed inputs for kernel accuracy, and Table 7 tensor shapes are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same smoothing, quantization-format/granularity, accumulator, kernel-error, and adaptive-selection analyses remain in Tables 1–5 and 9–11. The qualitative examples and outlier visualizations are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same average/worst-layer summaries. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged, with no added or removed result entries. For example, both report CogvideoX at 327.57 TOPS with a 2.01x speedup in Table 7 and SageAttention's Llama2 WikiText perplexity as 5.824 in Table 8.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, Equations (1)–(6), and softmax-invariance argument for centering K are unchanged. Adding missing transposes to QK in prose aligns notation with the existing equations rather than changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: plug-and-play attention quantization, approximately 2.1x/2.7x acceleration over FlashAttention2/xformers, and negligible end-to-end accuracy loss.

C2.justification: Outlier explanations, quantization failure conditions, speed–accuracy interpretations, and the deferred Hopper implementation remain unchanged. Removing RTX3090 from one illustrative INT8-versus-FP8 sentence does not establish a revised applicability boundary; the broader hardware discussion is retained.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1's corrected key/value load indices make the implementation instructions internally consistent. Triton and Tensor Core details, hardware disclosures, tensor shapes, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged; the correction does not establish a changed implementation or rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. Rewording FlashAttention3's Hopper exclusivity repeats the existing positioning rather than introducing a new comparison or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 adds Haofeng Huang to the author list, makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, and adjusts paragraph breaks. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables shift with text reflow, notably Figure 7 moving from page 8 to page 9. Figure assets, axes, legends, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1's inner-loop key/value load indices removes a concrete inconsistency and makes the pseudocode more reliable to follow. The remaining changes are principally editorial and layout adjustments; the empirical evidence and conclusions are unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
